docRequirement: changelog.md:41 (v2.1.219, July 24 2026): "Subagents can now spawn nested subagents up to depth 3 by default (was 1); set CLAUDE\_CODE\_MAX\_SUBAGENT\_SPAWN\_DEPTH=1 to disable nesting". The binding has two halves. (a) The DEFAULT number of subagent layers below the main conversation is 3, not 1 — env-vars.md:280 fixes the semantics: "Number of subagent layers allowed below the main conversation (default: 3). At the default, subagents can spawn their own subagents, and a subagent at the third layer can't spawn further; set `1` to turn nesting off." (b) The limit is USER-CONFIGURABLE through the env var `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH`, settable from the `env` block of `settings.json` (sub-agents.md:867-874), which "Accepts a positive whole number in plain digits; anything else is ignored, so the limit can be adjusted but not removed" (env-vars.md:280).
current: Our ceiling is 1 layer and there is no override on any user-reachable surface. (2) Enforced in `spawnChildSession`: `spawner.ts:517` computes `const depth = (args.depth ?? 0) + 1`, `:518-519` `if (depth > (cfg.maxDepth ?? DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH)) return failure(args.agentDef.name, `Subagent depth limit exceeded (${cfg.maxDepth ?? DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH})`)`. Our `depth`/`maxDepth` counting is layers-below-main, identical to the page's, so 1 vs 3 is a like-for-like value gap. (9) Documented as 1 in `packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:47` — "| `depth` | `1` | ... Default is ONE level of delegation; raise it explicitly for deeper trees."
divergence: Two deltas, one value and one missing mechanism. (a) VALUE: the default layer count is 1 where the page says 3. The key name, the counting convention (layers below the main conversation) and the at-limit enforcement point are all already right — only the number is wrong, in four places that must move together (`spawner.ts:110`, `harness-manifest.ts:107`, `SessionManager.ts:4932`, and the two tests that pin them). (b) MECHANISM: there is no configurable limit at all. Claude exposes it as `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` (env or `settings.json` `env` block), so `1` is the documented OPT-OUT and any positive integer is settable; we expose it only as `orchestrator.depth` on the internal execution manifest, which no production path writes, so neither a user nor an admin can change nesting depth by any means. Note what is NOT part of this delta: at-limit behaviour differs separately and knowingly — sub-agents.md:861 says Claude "withholds the `Agent` tool from every subagent except a fork" while we always return the `Subagent depth limit exceeded (N)` error from the call site (`spawner.ts:513-519` records that choice, which matches only the documented FORK behaviour). Raising the default to 3 does not fix that, and does not depend on it.

blastRadius: Crosses three packages and BOTH a wire and a persistence boundary — a risk trigger in this repo. (1) Wire: `PiChildBudgetsV1.maxDepth` (`packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/child-session-port.ts:8`) is a required field the host sends on every `port.start`, produced at `spawner.ts:602` and re-derived on the host at `SessionManager.ts:4932`, `:11141`, `:11216`. No schema change — only the default value written into it moves. (2) Persistence: the same object is stored on the session record (`packages/shared/src/sessions/types.ts:398`, key listed in the store-v2 field set at `:48`, cloned at `SessionManager.ts:9298`, `:10474`), so new records carry `maxDepth: 3` while resumed old records keep 1; no migration needed, but a resumed pre-change child keeps the old ceiling only insofar as anything reads the record's value — today the child's effective ceiling comes from its own manifest (`orchestrator.depth`), not from the persisted budget, so the persisted number is record/telemetry state. (3) Manifest: `PiOrchestratorConfig.depth` already exists and is already enumerated by the harness contract baseline (`packages/pi-agent-server/src/__tests__/harness-contract/pi-harness-baseline.test.ts:397` `orchestratorFields`, with a fixture using `depth: 2` at :326), so adding it to the seed adds no field and needs no surfaceVersion bump. It is NOT in any tool schema, so the `modelContractHash` / 'Pi execution manifest model contract mismatch' hazard that forced `maxParallelTasks` out of the schema does not apply. (4) Spawn consumers of the ceiling: `subagent-tool.ts` (`depth` at :464, :525), `workflow-tool.ts:605`, `review-tool.ts`, `guardian-runner.ts` — all reach `spawnChildSession` through `SpawnChildSessionArgs`, 22 call sites per codegraph, so all of them gain two more layers of headroom at once. (5) Tests that would go red or need review: `spawner.test.ts`, `harness-manifest.test.ts`, `subagent-tool.test.ts:411`, `subtask.test.ts`, `SessionManager.orchestration.test.ts`, `SessionManager.fork-subagent.test.ts`, `fork-parent-scope.test.ts`, `SessionManager.plugin-hook-runners.test.ts:474`, `child-session-service.test.ts` (most set explicit `maxDepth` fixtures and are unaffected; the two lockstep assertions are the ones that must change). (6) Imported Claude plugin/agent definitions that assume depth-3 nesting become functional; nothing about the fork rule changes — `isForkSession` (`spawner.ts:96-100`, `:502-505`) is unconditional and is not derived from the depth budget. (7) Concurrency interaction: a 3-layer tree multiplies live children against the same global semaphore (`concurrency`, default 16, narrowed to `min(concurrency, cpuCores - 2)`), which is the real cost of this change and the reason the 5→1 lowering happened in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-subagent-trust.md`.
userImpact: Observable today, and it silently truncates delegation trees. Any subagent that itself delegates fails: the second-layer `subagent` call returns `Subagent depth limit exceeded (1)` in the transcript, so the documented pattern from sub-agents.md — 'a reviewer subagent that dispatches a verifier per finding' — cannot run on Nessy at all; the top-level subagent either does the work itself or reports the error. The same applies to a `workflow` run started inside a subagent: `workflow-tool.ts:605` passes the session depth, so its `agent()` calls land at depth 2 and are refused. Imported Claude agent definitions and plugins written against the current default (3) therefore misbehave here in a way that reads like a plugin bug rather than a configuration difference. Second, there is no escape hatch: a user or admin who reads Claude's docs and sets `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` (or any `NESSY_*` guess) in the environment or in settings sees no effect whatsoever, because nothing reads any depth env var and the only knob, `orchestrator.depth`, is an internal manifest field no production path writes.
